spec.description: How warm or cool each room of Newcastle University's Urban Sciences Building feels, floor by floor: the thermal sensation ISO 7730 predicts (PMV, cold −3 to hot +3) from each room's live temperature and humidity, for the clothes and activity you pick, and the share of people who would be uncomfortable (PPD). Readings from the Urban Observatory's open stream, as Pacha's recorder keeps them; brush the week to move the map.

spec.rawSql:
-- The readings: what the building's sensors pushed, kept by Pacha's recorder (files: the hours
-- of the time range and the six before it, since a sensor sends a value only when it changes),
-- tied to their room by the BMS point (points.parquet).
SET VARIABLE t0 = to_timestamp(CAST(${__from} AS BIGINT) / 1000);
SET VARIABLE t1 = to_timestamp(CAST(${__to} AS BIGINT) / 1000);
WITH s AS (
  SELECT r.ts, r.point, r.value, p.kind, u.room_key, u.level
  FROM read_parquet([${files:singlequote}]) r
  JOIN read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/urban-sciences-building/points.parquet') p USING (point)
  JOIN read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/urban-sciences-building/rooms.parquet') u USING (entity_id)
  WHERE r.ts <= getvariable('t1') AND p.kind IN ('temp', 'rh', 'occupancy')
)
-- The newest reading recorded: the stream sends a value within minutes on a working day.
SELECT max(ts) AS latest FROM s

spec.description: When the newest reading was recorded. The building sends a value when it changes, within minutes on a working day; much older means the stream or the recorder has stopped.
spec.title: Latest reading

spec.rawSql:
-- Each room at the window's end: its latest hour at or before t1 (the Time Brush's window).
WITH now AS (
  SELECT c.*, p.room, p.level, p.floor_name, p.area_m2
  FROM $comfort c JOIN $plan p USING (room_key)
  WHERE c.time <= CAST(replace(replace(${t1:sqlstring}, 'T', ' '), 'Z', '') AS TIMESTAMP)
  QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY c.room_key ORDER BY c.time DESC) = 1
)
SELECT round(avg(ppd)) AS ppd FROM now p WHERE (${floor:sqlstring} = '' OR p.level = try_cast(${floor:sqlstring} AS INTEGER))

spec.description: The PPD of ISO 7730: the share of people who would find their room too warm or too cool, on average over the rooms with a reading on the floor picked, now. 5 % is the least any room can do; the standard's best buildings stay under 6 %, good ones under 10 %, acceptable ones under 15 %.
spec.title: Would be uncomfortable

spec.rawSql:
-- Each room at the window's end: its latest hour at or before t1 (the Time Brush's window).
WITH now AS (
  SELECT c.*, p.room, p.level, p.floor_name, p.area_m2
  FROM $comfort c JOIN $plan p USING (room_key)
  WHERE c.time <= CAST(replace(replace(${t1:sqlstring}, 'T', ' '), 'Z', '') AS TIMESTAMP)
  QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY c.room_key ORDER BY c.time DESC) = 1
)
SELECT round(avg(pmv), 1) AS pmv FROM now p WHERE (${floor:sqlstring} = '' OR p.level = try_cast(${floor:sqlstring} AS INTEGER))

spec.description: The mean PMV of the rooms with a reading on the floor picked, at the end of the window, in the words of ISO 7730's scale.
spec.title: Feels, on average

spec.rawSql:
-- Each room at the window's end: its latest hour at or before t1 (the Time Brush's window).
WITH now AS (
  SELECT c.*, p.room, p.level, p.floor_name, p.area_m2
  FROM $comfort c JOIN $plan p USING (room_key)
  WHERE c.time <= CAST(replace(replace(${t1:sqlstring}, 'T', ' '), 'Z', '') AS TIMESTAMP)
  QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY c.room_key ORDER BY c.time DESC) = 1
),
-- The room the charts follow: the one clicked on the map or in the table, or else the one that
-- feels coolest on the floor picked at the window's end.
focus AS (
  SELECT room_key FROM now p
  WHERE room_key = ${room:sqlstring} OR (${room:sqlstring} = '' AND (${floor:sqlstring} = '' OR p.level = try_cast(${floor:sqlstring} AS INTEGER)))
  ORDER BY room_key = ${room:sqlstring} DESC, pmv LIMIT 1
)
SELECT n.room || ', ' || lower(n.floor_name) || ' (' || n.area_m2 || ' m²)' AS room
FROM now n JOIN focus USING (room_key)

spec.description: The room clicked on the map or in the table; until then, the one that feels coolest on the floor picked at the end of the window.
spec.title: The charts follow

options.content:
## About the data

**How a room feels** is the PMV, the predicted mean vote of ISO 7730 (and ASHRAE 55): Fanger's model of the heat a person
gains and loses in a room, turned into the vote people give on a seven-point scale, from −3 cold through 0 neutral to +3 hot.
It takes the air's temperature and humidity, measured, and four things it cannot measure, assumed here: the walls at the air's
temperature, still air (0.1 m/s), and the clothes and activity picked at the top (a jumper and desk work at first). Change them
and every room feels different: the same 19.8 °C is neutral in a jumper and cool in a shirt. **PPD** is the share of people
who would be uncomfortable at that PMV, 5 % at best. The PMV here is checked against the standard's own examples (22 °C,
60 %, 1.2 met, 0.5 clo: −0.75, 17 %). A room without a humidity sensor is given 35 %, the building's usual.

**The building** is Newcastle University's Urban Sciences Building (2017, seven floors), home of the Urban Observatory. The
rooms and walls come from the building's own model, as in the dashboard
[Urban Sciences Building, room by room](/d/urban-sciences-building), which shows the same rooms by their CO2.

**The readings** are live: the building management system pushes each sensor's value when it changes, over the Urban
Observatory's open stream (wss://api.usb.urbanobservatory.ac.uk/stream, CC BY 4.0), and Pacha's recorder keeps a week of it.
A value holds until the next one: each room is read at the middle of every hour, and that week, with its PMV, loads
once into your browser (Chaski), where the map, the cards and the charts query it. Only floors 1 and 2 send temperatures today (about 40 rooms and zones); the others stopped
in 2025. The recording starts when the recorder does: there is no history before it.

Data: Urban Observatory, Newcastle University, CC BY 4.0. PMV and PPD: ISO 7730:2005, computed in DuckDB.

spec.rawSql:
-- The week hour by hour: the share of rooms with a reading that feel outside neutral (PMV beyond ±0.5).
SELECT time_bucket(INTERVAL 1 HOUR, time) AS time, round(100 * avg((abs(pmv) > 0.5)::INTEGER)) AS "Rooms outside neutral"
FROM $comfort GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

spec.description: The last 7 days, hour by hour: the share of rooms with a reading that feel outside neutral (PMV beyond ±0.5) for the clothes and activity picked. Its window is the hour on the map, the cards and the table: drag it, step it hour by hour, or press play; everything is in your browser, so it moves at once. The charts below show the whole week.
spec.title: Hours on the map

spec.rawSql:
-- For each floor, the mean PMV of its rooms with a reading, hour by hour over the week.
SELECT c.time,
       avg(c.pmv) FILTER (WHERE p.level = 0) AS "Ground",
       avg(c.pmv) FILTER (WHERE p.level = 1) AS "Floor 1",
       avg(c.pmv) FILTER (WHERE p.level = 2) AS "Floor 2",
       avg(c.pmv) FILTER (WHERE p.level = 3) AS "Floor 3",
       avg(c.pmv) FILTER (WHERE p.level = 4) AS "Floor 4",
       avg(c.pmv) FILTER (WHERE p.level = 5) AS "Floor 5",
       avg(c.pmv) FILTER (WHERE p.level = 6) AS "Floor 6"
FROM $comfort c JOIN $plan p USING (room_key)
GROUP BY c.time ORDER BY c.time

spec.description: For each floor, the mean PMV of its rooms with a reading, hour by hour over the week: between the dashed lines (−0.5 to +0.5) is what ISO 7730 calls neutral. Only floors 1 and 2 send temperatures.
spec.title: How each floor feels

spec.rawSql:
-- Every room with sensors, every hour of the week, coloured by how it feels then: the map's time
-- filter (the Time Brush's window, t0 to t1) keeps the hour it shows, so moving the window queries
-- nothing. Rooms without a reading this week, once, in grey (no time: the filter leaves them).
SELECT p.room_key, p.room, p.level, p.floor_name, c.time, c.temp_c, c.rh_pct, c.pmv, c.ppd,
       c.feels, p.area_m2, p.geometry
FROM $comfort c JOIN $plan p USING (room_key)
UNION ALL
SELECT p.room_key, p.room, p.level, p.floor_name, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, 'No reading', p.area_m2, p.geometry
FROM $plan p WHERE p.room_key NOT IN (SELECT room_key FROM $comfort)
ORDER BY time NULLS FIRST

-- The rest of each floor: corridors, stairs, plant and the rooms the API does not list.
SELECT room, level, floor_name, geometry FROM $shell WHERE part = 'rest'

-- Each floor's outline, the slab its rooms stand on.
SELECT level, floor_name, geometry FROM $shell WHERE part = 'floor'

-- The internal walls of each floor, from the building's model, drawn 1.2 m high.
SELECT level, floor_name, height_m, geometry FROM $shell WHERE part = 'wall'

-- The names of the rooms with no temperature reading this week (those with one carry their name
-- under their dial).
SELECT short AS label, level, latitude, longitude
FROM $plan WHERE named AND room_key NOT IN (SELECT room_key FROM $comfort)

-- A dial per room with a temperature, every hour of the week: the map's time filter (the Time
-- Brush's window, t0 to t1) keeps the hour it shows, and the room's card charts the whole week.
-- Under the ring the room's name and that hour's temperature (a blank first line keeps them under it).
SELECT chr(10) || p.short || chr(10) || printf('%.1f °C', c.temp_c) AS label,
       p.room, p.level, c.time, c.pmv, c.feels, c.ppd, c.temp_c, c.rh_pct, p.latitude, p.longitude
FROM $comfort c JOIN $plan p USING (room_key)
ORDER BY c.time

spec.description: The building's floors, stacked: pick one on the map's floor picker (it shows, per floor, the share of people who would be uncomfortable, on average over the week) and the others fade. Rooms are coloured by how they would feel at the end of the window brushed above, for the clothes and activity picked; a dial per room gives its PMV then, with its temperature under it, and its card charts the room's week. Rooms without a reading in grey, corridors, stairs and plant in white. Click a room for the charts below.
spec.title: How every room feels, floor by floor

-- Each room at the window's end: its latest hour at or before t1 (the Time Brush's window).
WITH now AS (
  SELECT c.*, p.room, p.level, p.floor_name, p.area_m2
  FROM $comfort c JOIN $plan p USING (room_key)
  WHERE c.time <= CAST(replace(replace(${t1:sqlstring}, 'T', ' '), 'Z', '') AS TIMESTAMP)
  QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY c.room_key ORDER BY c.time DESC) = 1
),
-- The room the charts follow: the one clicked on the map or in the table, or else the one that
-- feels coolest on the floor picked at the window's end.
focus AS (
  SELECT room_key FROM now p
  WHERE room_key = ${room:sqlstring} OR (${room:sqlstring} = '' AND (${floor:sqlstring} = '' OR p.level = try_cast(${floor:sqlstring} AS INTEGER)))
  ORDER BY room_key = ${room:sqlstring} DESC, pmv LIMIT 1
)

SELECT c.time, c.pmv AS "PMV", c.temp_c AS "Temperature", c.occupied AS "Occupied"

spec.description: How the room named above feels over the week (PMV, left axis, neutral between the dashed lines), with its temperature (right axis) and, bars, the hours its occupancy sensor saw someone.

-- Each room at the window's end: its latest hour at or before t1 (the Time Brush's window).
WITH now AS (
  SELECT c.*, p.room, p.level, p.floor_name, p.area_m2
  FROM $comfort c JOIN $plan p USING (room_key)
  WHERE c.time <= CAST(replace(replace(${t1:sqlstring}, 'T', ' '), 'Z', '') AS TIMESTAMP)

query.rawSql:
-- PMV, the thermal sensation ISO 7730 predicts (Fanger's model: -3 cold, 0 neutral, +3 hot), for a
-- room's air temperature (ta, °C) and humidity (rh, %), with the walls at the air's temperature, still
-- air (0.1 m/s), and the clothing (clo) and activity (met) picked above. The clothing's surface
-- temperature is found by 40 steps of the standard's iteration. PPD: the share of people who would
-- be uncomfortable at that PMV, 5 % at best.
CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP MACRO pmv(ta, rh, vel, met, clo) AS (
  WITH k AS (SELECT
      rh * 10 * exp(16.6536 - 4030.183 / (ta + 235)) AS pa,
      0.155 * clo AS icl, met * 58.15 AS m,
      CASE WHEN 0.155 * clo <= 0.078 THEN 1 + 1.29 * 0.155 * clo ELSE 1.05 + 0.645 * 0.155 * clo END AS fcl,
      12.1 * sqrt(vel) AS hcf, ta + 273 AS taa),
  p AS (SELECT *, icl * fcl * 3.96 AS p2, icl * fcl * 100 AS p3, icl * fcl * taa AS p4,
               308.7 - 0.028 * m + icl * fcl * 3.96 * pow(taa / 100, 4) AS p5,
               taa + (35.5 - ta) / (3.5 * icl + 0.1) AS tcla FROM k),
  it AS (SELECT *, list_reduce(list_transform(range(40), lambda i: {'xf': 0.0::DOUBLE, 'xn': 0.0::DOUBLE}), lambda acc, e:
            {'xf': (acc.xf + acc.xn) / 2,
             'xn': (p5 + p4 * greatest(hcf, 2.38 * pow(abs(100 * (acc.xf + acc.xn) / 2 - taa), 0.25))
                    - p2 * pow((acc.xf + acc.xn) / 2, 4))
                   / (100 + p3 * greatest(hcf, 2.38 * pow(abs(100 * (acc.xf + acc.xn) / 2 - taa), 0.25)))},
            {'xf': (tcla / 50)::DOUBLE, 'xn': (tcla / 100)::DOUBLE}) AS r FROM p),
  h AS (SELECT *, r.xn AS xn, 100 * r.xn - 273 AS tcl,
               greatest(hcf, 2.38 * pow(abs(100 * r.xn - taa), 0.25)) AS hc FROM it)
  SELECT (0.303 * exp(-0.036 * m) + 0.028) * (m
      - 3.05e-3 * (5733 - 6.99 * m - pa)
      - CASE WHEN m > 58.15 THEN 0.42 * (m - 58.15) ELSE 0 END
      - 1.7e-5 * m * (5867 - pa)
      - 0.0014 * m * (34 - ta)
      - 3.96 * fcl * (pow(xn, 4) - pow(taa / 100, 4))
      - fcl * hc * (tcl - ta)) FROM h);
CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP MACRO ppd(x) AS 100 - 95 * exp(-0.03353 * pow(x, 4) - 0.2179 * pow(x, 2));
-- A room's PMV with the clothes and activity picked; a room without a humidity sensor is given
-- 35 %, the building's usual (PMV moves by under 0.1 for 10 points of humidity here).
CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP MACRO feel(ta, rh) AS pmv(ta, coalesce(rh, 35), 0.1, CAST(${met:sqlstring} AS DOUBLE), CAST(${clo:sqlstring} AS DOUBLE));
-- The words of ISO 7730's seven-point scale, each PMV to the nearest one.
CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP MACRO feels(x) AS CASE WHEN x IS NULL THEN NULL
  WHEN x < -2.5 THEN 'Cold' WHEN x < -1.5 THEN 'Cool' WHEN x < -0.5 THEN 'Slightly cool'
  WHEN x <= 0.5 THEN 'Neutral' WHEN x <= 1.5 THEN 'Slightly warm' WHEN x <= 2.5 THEN 'Warm' ELSE 'Hot' END;

-- Server side: the last 7 days of the building's rooms, hour by hour, from Pacha's recorder (a
-- sensor sends a value only when it changes, so the files start six hours earlier): each room's
-- temperature, humidity and occupancy at the middle of every hour (its latest value then; of two
-- sensors of a kind, the mean), and how it feels for the clothes and activity picked. time is the
-- middle of the hour, so a one-hour window of the Time Brush holds one row per room.
SET VARIABLE files = (SELECT list(url) FROM read_json('http://feeds/recordings/urban-sciences-building/manifest.json',
                                                      columns = {url: 'VARCHAR', "from": 'TIMESTAMPTZ', "to": 'TIMESTAMPTZ'})
                      WHERE "to" >= now() - INTERVAL 7 DAY - INTERVAL 6 HOUR);
WITH s AS (
  SELECT r.ts, r.value, p.kind, u.room_key
  FROM read_parquet(getvariable('files')) r
  JOIN read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/urban-sciences-building/points.parquet') p USING (point)
  JOIN read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/urban-sciences-building/rooms.parquet') u USING (entity_id)
  WHERE p.kind IN ('temp', 'rh', 'occupancy')
),
k AS (SELECT room_key, kind, ts, avg(value) AS value FROM s GROUP BY ALL),
hours AS (SELECT unnest(generate_series(date_trunc('hour', now() - INTERVAL 7 DAY), now(), INTERVAL 1 HOUR)) + INTERVAL 30 MINUTE AS t),
g AS (SELECT room_key, t FROM (SELECT DISTINCT room_key FROM s WHERE kind = 'temp'), hours WHERE t <= now()),
hr AS (
  SELECT g.room_key, g.t, tp.value AS temp, rh.value AS rh, oc.value AS occupancy FROM g
  ASOF LEFT JOIN (SELECT * FROM k WHERE kind = 'temp') tp ON g.room_key = tp.room_key AND g.t >= tp.ts
  ASOF LEFT JOIN (SELECT * FROM k WHERE kind = 'rh') rh ON g.room_key = rh.room_key AND g.t >= rh.ts
  ASOF LEFT JOIN (SELECT * FROM k WHERE kind = 'occupancy') oc ON g.room_key = oc.room_key AND g.t >= oc.ts
)
SELECT room_key, t AS time, round(temp, 1) AS temp_c, round(rh) AS rh_pct,
       CASE WHEN occupancy IS NULL THEN NULL WHEN occupancy >= 0.5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS occupied,
       round(pmv, 2) AS pmv, round(ppd(pmv)) AS ppd, feels(pmv) AS feels
FROM (SELECT *, feel(temp, rh) AS pmv FROM hr WHERE temp IS NOT NULL)
ORDER BY time, room_key

-- Server side: every room the Urban Observatory has sensors for, from the building's plan
-- (datasets/urban-sciences-building): its outline, a point inside it for its dial, its floor (level 0
-- the ground floor) and its name, short for a zone of an open-plan room (Z5).
SELECT u.room_key, u.label AS room, u.room IS NOT NULL AS named,
       CASE WHEN u.room LIKE '% Zone %' THEN 'Z' || split_part(u.room, ' Zone ', 2) ELSE u.room END AS short,
       u.level, CASE u.floor WHEN 'G' THEN 'Ground' ELSE 'Floor ' || u.floor END AS floor_name, round(u.area_m2) AS area_m2,
       ST_AsGeoJSON(ST_GeomFromText(u.wkt))::VARCHAR AS geometry,
       ST_Y(ST_PointOnSurface(ST_GeomFromText(u.wkt))) AS latitude,
       ST_X(ST_PointOnSurface(ST_GeomFromText(u.wkt))) AS longitude
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/urban-sciences-building/rooms.parquet') u
WHERE u.entity_id IS NOT NULL

-- Server side: what does not change on the map, once: the rest of each floor (corridors, stairs,
-- plant and the rooms the API does not list), each floor's outline (the slab its rooms stand on) and
-- the internal walls, drawn 1.2 m high, from the building's model (datasets/urban-sciences-building).
SELECT 'rest' AS part, coalesce(u.label, 'Corridor, stairs or plant') AS room, u.level,
       CASE u.floor WHEN 'G' THEN 'Ground' ELSE 'Floor ' || u.floor END AS floor_name, NULL::DOUBLE AS height_m,
       ST_AsGeoJSON(ST_GeomFromText(u.wkt))::VARCHAR AS geometry
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/urban-sciences-building/rooms.parquet') u WHERE u.entity_id IS NULL
UNION ALL
SELECT 'floor', NULL, u.level, CASE u.floor WHEN 'G' THEN 'Ground' ELSE 'Floor ' || u.floor END, NULL,
       ST_AsGeoJSON(ST_GeomFromText(u.wkt))::VARCHAR
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/urban-sciences-building/floors.parquet') u
UNION ALL
SELECT 'wall', NULL, u.level, CASE u.floor WHEN 'G' THEN 'Ground' ELSE 'Floor ' || u.floor END, 1.2,
       ST_AsGeoJSON(ST_GeomFromText(u.wkt))::VARCHAR
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/urban-sciences-building/walls.parquet') u
